notes: USMLE Content Outline 2026 page 37 was inspected directly and includes confidence intervals, statistical versus clinical significance, and application of study results to patient care.
USMLE Content Outline 2026 page 39 was inspected directly and includes health literacy/numeracy and patient-centered information provision.
Current CDC Field Epidemiology Manual guidance supports interpreting a confidence interval as values consistent with the data and using interval width to assess precision.
NIST directly supports the repeated-sampling interpretation of a 95% confidence level and therefore the rejection of a posterior-probability interpretation.
AHRQ methods guidance supports classifying a wide interval spanning clinically distinct conclusions as imprecise.
The initial wording 'meaningful reduction' was removed before PASS because the vignette did not specify a clinical-importance threshold.

official_outline_path: Study interpretation, drawing conclusions from data — confidence intervals
Clinical decision making, interpretation and use of evidence-based data and recommendations
Social Sciences — Communication and interpersonal skills, including health literacy and numeracy — information provision

duplicate_gate.ppv_rejected_overlap: Canonical Q0091 directly tests positive predictive value versus prevalence

claim_audit.rr_null_value: PASS — for a relative risk the null value is 1.0.
claim_audit.ci_crosses_null: PASS — 0.70 to 1.16 includes 1.0 and values on both sides.
claim_audit.wide_ci_imprecision: PASS — CDC/AHRQ support interval width as a measure of precision and wide intervals as imprecise.
claim_audit.null_not_proven: PASS — inclusion of the null means the data are compatible with the null, not that no effect is proven.
claim_audit.frequentist_interpretation: PASS — NIST supports repeated-sampling coverage rather than assigning a 95% posterior probability to the fixed true effect.
claim_audit.communication: PASS — the answer gives a direct, numeracy-appropriate explanation of what the study can and cannot establish.

option_audit.correct: Accurately communicates point estimate plus uncertainty without overstating benefit, null effect, or harm.
option_audit.point_estimate_only: Incorrectly treats the point estimate as proof and ignores interval uncertainty.
option_audit.null_proven: Incorrectly equates inclusion of 1.0 with proof of no effect.
option_audit.posterior_probability: Incorrect frequentist interpretation of the observed 95% CI.
option_audit.probability_no_effect: Incorrectly converts null inclusion into a 95% probability of ineffectiveness.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: RR 0.90 with 95% CI 0.70–1.16 gives a point estimate below 1 but an interval spanning lower risk, no difference, and higher risk. The proper clinical communication is uncertainty/imprecision, not proof in either direction.
adversarial_second_pass.q0627_overlap_attack: Q0627 tests absolute-risk framing and consistent denominators; Q0657 tests interpretation and communication of an imprecise confidence interval. Constructs are distinct.
adversarial_second_pass.q0091_overlap_attack: Q0091 tests predictive value versus prevalence; Q0657 does not test PPV.
adversarial_second_pass.probability_attack: The correct answer avoids the common but incorrect statement that there is a 95% probability the fixed true effect lies inside this particular observed interval.
adversarial_second_pass.clinical_significance_attack: No 'clinically meaningful' threshold is asserted after correction.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The hypothetical RR and CI are self-contained study data; no real-world drug efficacy, event rate, sample size, p-value, treatment duration, or external numerical claim is asserted.

note: Approved after broad construct-aware duplicate rejection of overlapping PPV/risk-framing concepts, official USMLE verification, CDC/AHRQ/NIST statistical interpretation review, wording correction, post-correction SQLite rerun, and independent adversarial second-pass.
